coordinate_frame: Workstation metres, +X east, +Y north, +Z up; radians; wxyz quaternions
objective: Complete the declared assembly/transport task correctly and efficiently; allocation, local motion and collaboration are Agent choices.
rules: Move all 2 numbered payload assemblies from their individual initial positions toward the common GOAL. START marks the route origin; returning scattered payloads to START is not required.
Route regions and arrows indicate progress. Grasp points, handover locations, robot teams, allocation and execution order are planner choices. Independent work may run concurrently.
Grasp the red timber, not a pendant, ring or shaft. Keep the whole assembly clear of table and floor during airborne transport, except for the allowed final GOAL landing.
Any final placement in GOAL is allowed, including cargo contact and stacking. Oracle packing centers and contact-free separation are not task requirements.

The complete assembly must be within the GOAL outline with at most 50mm outward geometric tolerance on each boundary. Final completion requires actual release from every robot and actual table support, directly or through other accepted cargo. There is no additional velocity threshold or stationary-duration requirement.
Only ordinary robot actuators and real contacts may change the live task. No hand welds, object-state writes, hidden-state tools, runtime physics changes or stabilizing attachments.

The initial endpoint chord is 1.15m. The underside fixed eye is 100mm along the timber from its end and directly interlinks with a free eye; the wooden pendant shaft is 170mm long and carries a 600g weight. There is no mounting stem, cable or tray.
The rigid circular-arc timber subtends 63 degrees.
Collisions, drops and other process events are recorded separately. Recover using ordinary robot actions; do not reset, respawn or erase history.

completion.scope: All assemblies released, actually supported and inside GOAL tolerance; process events are reported separately.

mechanism.collision: 32 tangent convex segments; smooth visual sweep; analytic arc mass distributed over segments
mechanism.suspension: Underside direct fixed eye, physically contact-linked free eye,170mm wooden shaft and600g weight; no bracket, cable or weld

rigid_suspension_profile.weight_material: Steel calibration-weight form; nominal manufactured mass, not a measured specimen

mechanism.initial_condition: Table-supported tilted beam and directly mounted underside eye; independent wooden pendulum lies on tabletop. No added support fixtures.

pendulum.connection: Closed contact-linked eyes; independent free weight body

mechanism.finish: Tabletop destination region; no cradle; beam and suspended assembly must land stably
mechanism.initial_distribution: Separate positions along the route; each travels rightward to the common destination

presentation.opening: L2/L3 whole assembly yaw reversed by180 degrees; opening faces the original local route-forward direction
presentation.physics_scope: R16 user-requested apparatus replacement; unchanged robot mounts, worktop, robot controllers, timestep and goal acceptance. Timber shape, suspension and L3 hinge direction follow the new declared geometry.

family_guidance:
# Air Relay — terminal outcome v2

Read the assigned task and move every assembly from its initial position to
GOAL. START marks the route origin; returning to START is not required. Choose
robot teams, route and any handovers based on available observations.

Completion requires every assembly to be released by all robots, actually
supported, and inside the GOAL boundary tolerance of 50 mm. Cargo contact and
stacking are allowed. Check the final physical state; opening alone does not
establish completion.

Collisions, drops and other process events are recorded separately from final
completion. You may observe and recover using ordinary robot actions. No reset,
respawn, state writing or history erasure is permitted.
